Stated Claim / Post Context:
Distinctive CC44 number plate fetches Dh6.72 million at lucrative Dubai auction | The National

Premium plate helps drive more than Dh65 million in sales

Actual Article Body:
UAE

October 27, 2026

A CC44 number plate sold for $1.8 million at Dubai's 121st RTA auction, making it the most expensive plate of the night.
The event generated $17.9 million in total sales across 60 rare number plates, featuring combinations across ten different letter codes.
Dubai's premium number plate market grows approximately 20 per cent annually, with $463 million in transactions recorded over the past three years.
The record for a single plate sale was set in April 2023, when an Emirati bidder paid $15 million for Dubai's coveted number 7 plate.
Dubai's private number plate market is set to gain its first escrow-backed online marketplace, with the Mazal app designed to "hold buyers' funds until ownership transfer is confirmed."

A motoring enthusiast is set to stand out in traffic after snapping up a distinctive CC44 vehicle number plate for Dh6.7 million ($1.8 million) at a lucrative auction in Dubai.

The major sale to the unnamed bidder proved to be the biggest of the night, as 60 rare number plates went under the hammer at an event held by the Roads and Transport Authority at Hilton Dubai Al Habtoor City at the weekend.

The auction amassed sales of Dh65.7 million, with CC44 leading the way, followed closely by BB18, which fetched Dh6.6 million, BB80, which sold for Dh5.9 million, and BB117, which went for Dh1 million.

Timeframe: When Abu Dhabi's number 1 plate set a world record

The open auction – the 121st organised by the RTA – featured three, four and five-digit combinations across the AA, BB, CC, H, U, V, W, X, Y and Z codes.

The success of the event served to highlight the enduring appeal of unique number plates for drivers keen to stand out from the crowd.

Bidders have shown they are prepared to dig deep to secure premium plates, with in-demand numbers selling for record prices. In April 2023, an Emirati bidder who paid a record Dh55 million for Dubai's number 7 plate at an auction for the One Billion Meals campaign.

That broke a record set in 2008, when businessman Saeed Al Khouri paid 50 times the opening Dh1 million bid for the coveted number 1 plate at a charity auction in Abu Dhabi.

Dubai's expanding vehicle premium market is poised to welcome the UAE's first escrow-backed online marketplace. The Mazal app will hold buyers’ funds until ownership transfer is confirmed, providing security to a second-hand market that has traditionally relied on social media, independent brokers and manual processes.

The platform aligns with RTA regulations, offering a secure marketplace with verified buyers and increasing confidence in high-value auctions.

Dubai’s private number plate market is growing by about 20 per cent a year, with single-digit and special-number plates commanding high values. In the past three years, Dubai’s status-symbol vehicle plate market has seen Dh1.7 billion in transactions, Mazal app data analysts have said. Mazal will manage these high-value transactions.
